prompt: What does it mean that a tree is built *greedily*?

choices.text: It grows until every leaf is pure
choices.why: That is having no brakes, not greed.

choices.text: It uses as many columns as it can
choices.why: Greed here is about the order of choices, not the number of columns.

choices.text: Each cut is the best available at that step, with no look-ahead
choices.why: Yes. A worse cut now that would allow better ones later is never tried.

choices.text: It always picks the column with the most distinct values first
choices.why: It picks the best cut, whichever column it is in.

prompt: Every leaf of `first_tree.py` says `class: 0`. Why is the tree still useful for sending credits?

choices.text: Class 0 means *send the credit*
choices.why: 0 is *stays*, the majority in every leaf.

choices.text: Because a deeper tree would change every class
choices.why: Depth is not the reason; probabilities are.

choices.text: It is not useful; a tree that never says *cancel* cannot pick anybody
choices.why: The class hides the probabilities, and those are what pick people.

choices.text: A leaf at 39% is above the 28% break-even
choices.why: Yes. The probabilities, not the class, decide the credit.

choices.text: A tree of depth 1 cannot be fitted
